name: fin_closed_periods
title: Closed Periods
description: A closed accounting period: from start_date through end_date inclusive, the books for that stretch are settled and no journal may be written, edited, or posted into it (hook-enforced on fin_journals and fin_journal_lines -- see the hooks' own docstrings). This is the control the predecessor system modeled (ClosedPeriod + period_locked) and most small-business books skip entirely: without it, last year's 'final' numbers stay quietly editable forever, which means the statements you filed and the statements you have can drift apart with nobody deciding they should. Closing a period is creating a row; reopening -- rare, and legitimate (a late auditor adjustment) -- is deleting it, and both land in the change log with an actor, so the question 'who reopened March?' has an answer. What this deliberately is NOT yet: year-end closing ENTRIES (moving net income to retained earnings -- fin_journals' reserved kind=closing, built when a real year-end needs it) and composer awareness (machine-composed journals write at the storage level, which bypasses hooks by design; a late bank-line resolution dated into a closed period is a real case that should surface to the operator rather than be silently blocked or silently shifted -- tracked in the package description until it repeats enough to earn its design).

fields.name: end_date
fields.label: Through
fields.help: Inclusive. A journal dated exactly on this date is inside the closed period.

fields.name: reason
fields.label: Reason
fields.help: Why this stretch is settled: 'FY2025 filed', 'Q2 reviewed'.

fields.name: closing_journal_id
fields.label: Closing Journal
fields.help: The year-end closing entry for this period, once closing entries exist. Optional until then.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.label: Entity
fields.help: Which set of books this closes. Blank closes the period for all of the owner's journals without an entity.
